A glowing green Doctor Doom face appears or scroll to the bottom of the search results page to spot a glowing green Doctor Doom icon.

, and the . Select any emblem to launch a quick, four- or five-question multiple-choice quiz generated by Google’s AI Mode, asking you to finish iconic quotes from that specific corner of the Marvel universe.

Article Title: Violent threats, public insults and a secret $1 million settlement: What former employees reveal about Nvidia's 'ousted' CEO Jensen Huang's way of running the company
Article Text:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Nvidia paid former HR chief Michael Winston over $1 million after he objected to Huang's conduct

Jensen Huang skipped one-on-one meetings and chose public humiliation over firing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter, faced similar complaints inside Nvidia

Jensen Huang once told Nvidia employees that they had become too rich to be motivated by money, so humiliation was the only way left to push them. That is one of several claims in a New York Times investigation into how the co-founder ran the world's most valuable chipmaker, published a week after he resigned as CEO. Based on more than a dozen current and former employees and two decades of court records, the report describes public tirades, violent threats and a confidential settlement of more than $1 million with a former HR head who said Huang "terrorized" staff.The threats, as described to the NYT, were oddly specific. Huang allegedly told one subordinate he would rip off both their arms and beat them to death with them, and told another he would tear off the top of their head and "pee on your brain." One witness said he told an executive that his mother should have aborted him."I'd rather torture you into greatness, because I believe in you," Huang once said.Huang stepped down last week after revelations of extramarital relationships, including one with a subordinate and another with a woman US intelligence believes is a Chinese intelligence asset. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the board has said it does not plan to reinstate him, even as thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for his return.Michael Winston joined Nvidia as senior vice president of human resources in September 2004. A month later, at an off-site with about 50 employees, he watched Huang threaten to rip out someone's heart and stomp on it, according to his notes reviewed by the NYT.Winston said he warned Huang that he was exposing Nvidia to lawsuits. Huang allegedly called public humiliation a "rite of passage" for new hires and said it had "good entertainment value."By November, Winston was fired and told he was "not a good fit." He said Huang warned him that if he sued, he would never work in Silicon Valley again. Winston filed a complaint with California's employment regulator and drafted a lawsuit, but both sides settled before it was filed, and neither admitted wrongdoing. The settlement had not been reported before. Winston died earlier this year.In 2007, former company lawyer Stephen Pettigrew also sued Nvidia, partly over retaliation for reporting Winston's allegations. That case settled in 2009.Huang avoided one-on-ones, saying they reduced transparency. Top executives saw it as a power play. Anyone who disagreed had to do it in front of a room, where Huang could ridicule them.When marketing executive Ned Finkle faltered in front of a major customer, Huang allegedly scolded him before the client, then moved him to government relations, a job Huang considered among Nvidia's least important. In 2019, after the company missed out on part of a US supercomputer contract, he tore into a sales executive in front of government officials. The executive threw his badge at Huang and quit on the spot.At Nvidia's developer conference this March, Huang repeatedly interrupted Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch over his French accent, telling him, "You're not even speaking human."Employees said the style rubbed off on other leaders, including Huang's daughter Madison, his de facto chief of staff, who still works at Nvidia. A separate NYT report said she berated colleagues senior to her. One of them was longtime lieutenant Jay Puri, on a call ahead of a February conference in New Delhi. Puri left his role less than six months later. HR put her through weekly coaching sessions, and one vice president dropped off her call citing an anxiety attack.Huang's spokesman John Fisher called Winston's claims "fabrications" from a fired employee. Nvidia declined to comment.
Article Summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly made violent threats to employees. He avoided one-on-one meetings and chose public humiliation over firing. Huang stepped down last week after revelations of extramarital relationships. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the board does not plan to reinstate him.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praises Jensen Huang but makes it clear that tech founders are not gods: ‘I used to tell Bill Gates…’
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Satya Nadella on why lasting companies need more than one leader

Satya Nadella credits Jensen Huang’s work at Nvidia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has weighed in on the cult of personality surrounding Silicon Valley founders, praising Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang for building an enduring company while reminding the tech world that founders, like Microsoft’s Bill Gates , are human and not gods. Speaking about the outsized influence individual entrepreneurs have on their companies, Nadella acknowledged that founders deserve celebration for doing something almost magical: creating something out of nothing. However, he pushed back against the extreme hero worship often seen in modern tech and capitalism.“So therefore, yes, they're singular. But they're not gods, right?. So I kind of feel at the end of the day, you know, as you know, I used to say to Bill [Gates] and everyone, like, founders also die,” Nadella said.In Nadella’s view, a founder’s real legacy isn't just the initial spark they bring to a business, but whether the organisation can stand on its own feet once they step away. For any company to succeed over the long haul, someone else eventually has to take the reins.“So, at some point, a company needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over and, in fact, the person who is going to be most happy about that will be the founder, because when the baby you sort of brought into the world is striving long after you're gone. That's really the institutional strength you build,” he explained.Nadella made it clear that he has little patience for executives who claim a business fell apart simply because they left.“I have never trusted any leader, founder or otherwise, who comes and says the institution after I left was completely gone. I mean, what the heck? Like, then what did you build?” he remarked.According to Nadella, true greatness in leadership comes down to balancing two things: the “magic” a founder creates at the start and the lasting “institutional strength” they leave behind.Pointing to Nvidia as a prime example of getting that balance right, Nadella credited Huang with building a resilient organisation capable of outlasting its founder. “And so I think that's what Jensen actually has done with Nvidia,” Nadella said.However, he stopped short of endorsing a potential comeback for the Nvidia co-founder. “I just want to give him space for what he needs to do there, and it's not up to me. It's up to the Nvidia board to decide what happens next,” Nadella said, adding that he has “all the admiration, respect for what Jensen has done for this industry, and what he's done for Nvidia, noting that the two have worked together for many years.”
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has weighed in on the cult of personality surrounding Silicon Valley founders. He praised Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang for building an enduring company while reminding the tech world that founders, like Microsoft’s Bill Gates, are human and not gods.

Article Title: As Florida uses robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons; study reveals when and how these python use trees
Article Text:
As Florida uses robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons; study reveals when and how these python use trees

Why smaller Burmese pythons climb trees more often

How Florida's robot rabbits help detect Burmese pythons

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

How many Burmese pythons have been removed in Florida

In 2025, Florida introduced solar-powered robot rabbits to tackle its growing population of invasive Burmese pythons. Now, a new study has revealed when and how these snakes climb trees, giving wildlife officials another clue to help locate and remove them. Researchers tracked 346 Burmese pythons, including 188 adults and 158 juveniles, in Big Cypress National Preserve between 2017 and 2024. According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the study recorded more than 4,000 habitat data points to understand how the snakes use their surroundings.The findings showed that Burmese pythons mostly stay on the ground, with less than 3% of all sightings involving tree climbing. However, around 17% of juvenile pythons and 14% of adult pythons were spotted climbing trees at least once during the study.Researchers found that juvenile pythons were more likely to climb trees than adults. Their smaller size and lighter weight may make it easier for them to move along branches. As a python grows heavier, its likelihood of climbing trees decreases. This means wildlife workers may need to look beyond the ground when searching for smaller invasive snakes.The findings could help improve python removal efforts because the snakes are already difficult to spot in Florida's dense vegetation.In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida introduced solar-powered robotic rabbit decoys to attract Burmese pythons. The robots mimic real prey by producing a heat signature and emitting a scent designed to attract snakes. They are also equipped with AI-powered cameras that monitor the surrounding area and alert officials when a python approaches. A trained removal agent can then be sent to capture the snake.“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district said.Burmese pythons are not native to Florida and are found in and around the Everglades, where they prey on birds, mammals and other reptiles, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC). Florida also organises the annual Florida Python Challenge, a 10-day competition that brings together professional and amateur hunters to capture the invasive snakes. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, removed 280 Burmese pythons.Since 2017, contractors working with the FWC and South Florida Water Management District have removed more than 19,000 snakes.The latest study adds to these efforts by showing that although most Burmese pythons remain on the ground, smaller snakes are more likely to climb trees.
Article Summary: Researchers tracked 346 Burmese pythons, including 188 adults and 158 juveniles, in Big Cypress National Preserve between 2017 and 2024. The study recorded more than 4,000 habitat data points to understand how the snakes use their surroundings. The findings could help improve python removal efforts because the snakes are already difficult to spot in Florida.

Article Title: AI just cracked math’s most famous problem, says Anthropic mathematician; here’s how Google CEO Sundar Pichai reacted
Article Text:
CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei.

A 167-year-old problem

Claude helped generate a massive proof

Google CEO Sundar Pichai’s reaction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The timing

Just days after Dario Amodei-led Anthropic made its historic public market debut, one of the company's mathematicians has made an even more extraordinary claim: that he has solved the Riemann Hypothesis, widely regarded as the most famous unsolved problem in mathematics, with the help of Anthropic's AI model Claude. According to a Wall Street Journal report cited by the user, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a landmark conjecture in number theory that has resisted attempts by mathematicians since it was first proposed in 1859.Proposed in 1859, the Riemann hypothesis has defeated the best human minds ever since. It became known as the field’s holy grail when it was chosen as one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in 2000, and even the most capable AI models hadn’t managed it. Alpöge posted his proof on his website in Lean, a programming language that lets computers check an argument line by line. Mathematicians immediately began working through it. He said the full argument is “incredibly long” and called the AI-written version “some massive unreadable travesty,” more than 250,000 pages.Alpöge revealed that the proof was developed with assistance from Claude, Anthropic's AI system.He published the work in Lean, a programming language and proof assistant designed to allow computers to verify mathematical arguments line by line. According to Alpöge, the complete proof is extraordinarily lengthy. He described the AI-generated version as an "incredibly long" argument spanning more than 250,000 pages. Mathematicians began reviewing the proof soon after it was published, attempting to verify whether the reasoning holds up under scrutiny. Importantly, the proof has not yet been formally accepted by the mathematical community. Independent verification will be required before the result can be considered proven.The announcement quickly drew attention across the technology industry, including from Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet. Reacting to the claim on X, Pichai wrote: "Somewhere Euler, Gauss and Riemann in awe today!" The remark referenced three of the most influential figures in mathematical history: Leonhard Euler, Carl Friedrich Gauss and Bernhard Riemann, whose work laid the foundations for large parts of modern mathematics.Alpöge said the result came late Sunday into Monday, days before Anthropic went public. He called the timing “horrible” and said he messaged CEO Dario Amodei to ask permission to announce it, noting there was a constraint to respect. Anthropic didn’t respond to a request for comment after his post, as its stock fell 13.04% on its first full day of trading.“I just could not live if I waited even longer,” he wrote. He added that he hoped the argument offers “a glimpse towards the miracles that lie ahead.”
Article Summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The conjecture is a landmark conjecture in number theory that has resisted attempts by mathematicians since it was first proposed in 1859. The proof was developed with assistance from Anthropic's AI system Claude.

Article Title: New York mayor Zohran Mamdani and Amazon are fighting again; says: It is Jeff Bezos' greed that is making the company charge …
Article Text:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani

Why is Amazon warning customers about a $5 delivery increase

What is New York City's Delivery Protection Act

Zohran Mamdani and Amazon clashed before

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has hit back at Amazon after the e-commerce giant began warning customers that their orders could cost up to $5 more if a proposed city law is passed. Calling the possible price increase an act of “greed”, Mamdani accused the company of using higher delivery costs to push back against legislation aimed at protecting workers and improving street safety. “Amazon is a multi-trillion dollar company. If Jeff Bezos adds $5 to your order, it’s not because of City Council's efforts to protect workers' rights and keep our streets safe. It's greed,” Zohran Mamdani wrote in a post on X. “Pass the Delivery Protection Act,” he added.The exchange marks another public clash between the mayor and Amazon, which has opposed the proposed legislation, arguing that it could disrupt its delivery network, increase costs and threaten thousands of jobs in New York City.Amazon began displaying messages on its website and mobile app on November 19, warning New York customers that the proposed Delivery Protection Act could add up to $5 to each order if passed in its current form. The company is also asking shoppers to contact their City Council representatives and oppose the bill. Its website and app provide a link through which customers can send messages to their elected representatives.Amazon said the proposed law could prevent it from continuing to work with the small delivery businesses it currently relies on. It also warned that it could be forced to consider moving its operations outside New York City, potentially making deliveries slower and more expensive.According to the company, around 20,000 New Yorkers used its link to contact City Council members in the first six hours of the campaign. Amazon later said more than 60,000 emails had been sent within the campaign's first 36 hours.An Amazon spokesperson said the company wanted customers to understand the possible financial impact of the legislation.“As the City Council continues to review this bill, we want to be transparent with our customers about what it would cost them if it passes as written – which is why we’re doing this,” spokesperson Kelly Nantel said, according to a New York Post report.The Delivery Protection Act, also known as Intro 518, is a proposed law aimed at changing how large delivery companies operate in New York City. The legislation, sponsored by City Council member Tiffany Cabán and backed by Mamdani, would introduce licensing requirements for last-mile delivery facilities and establish new worker safety, training and employment standards.It would also require companies operating these facilities, including Amazon, to directly employ workers involved in core delivery and warehouse services instead of relying on third-party contractors.Mamdani announced his support for the legislation in August, saying: “It's time to end the subcontracting model that puts profits over people and build an economy that works for working New Yorkers.”The latest disagreement is part of a series of disputes between Mamdani's administration and Amazon over the company's business practices, delivery operations and responsibility towards workers.In May 2026, the Mamdani administration announced that it had recovered more than $9 million from Amazon over unpaid fines linked to vehicle idling violations. The fines were connected to delivery vehicles operating through Amazon Logistics and its network of third-party transportation contractors. The city said Amazon had the largest outstanding amount under its idling laws.Reacting to the recovery, Mamdani said: “Amazon is worth $2 trillion. Yet, it did not deign to pay the millions of dollars it racked up in unpaid fines as its’ trucks illegally polluted our air and forced New Yorkers to breathe in their exhaust.We are going to collect every dollar they owe the people of this city.”In August, Zohran Mamdani's administration issued cease-and-desist orders to 42 online retailers, including Amazon, asking them to stop selling motorised e-bikes and scooters that allegedly violated New York City's safety and legal requirements. The city warned that retailers continuing to sell prohibited devices could face civil penalties of up to $2,000 for each illegal sale.
Article Summary: Amazon began displaying messages on its website and mobile app on November 19, warning New York customers that the proposed Delivery Protection Act could add up to $5 to each order if passed in its current form. The company is also asking shoppers to contact their City Council representatives and oppose the bill. Amazon said the proposed law could prevent it from continuing to work with the small delivery businesses it currently relies on.

Article Title: Meta threatens to pull WhatsApp from Canada; tells government: Your demands ignore software realities
Article Text:
Why technology companies are upset with Bill C-22

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Meta has warned Canadian lawmakers that it may consider pulling encrypted services from the country if the federal government passes its proposed lawful access legislation without further amendments. Speaking before a Senate committee reviewing Bill C-22, company representatives this week argued that the draft law would force technology companies to compromise digital security in order to comply with police warrants.Bill C-22, which passed the House of Commons in June, requires electronic service providers to adapt their systems so that they can hand over user data to investigators upon request. Critics say the mandate directly threatens end-to-end encryption, which is the security standard used by platforms like WhatsApp , Facebook, and Instagram to ensure messages can only be read by the sender and recipient."Ultimately, the Canadian government would be enforcing and imposing a law that it is not technically feasible to comply with and still offer secure, end-to-end encrypted services to Canadians," Robyn Greene, Meta’s director of privacy and public policy, testified before senators, according to a report in CBC.When pressed on whether the company would withdraw products from the Canadian market if the bill becomes law, Rachel Curran, Meta’s head of public policy for Canada, said the company would have to "review all of our options."Curran previously told Bloomberg that weakening encryption is a "red line" for Meta, warning the legislation risks turning private companies into "an arm of the government's surveillance apparatus. "The standoff centers on Part 2 of Bill C-22, which grants ministers the authority to issue confidential orders compelling tech companies to build law enforcement access capabilities into their platforms. The provision also allows the government to require companies to retain customer metadata—including IP addresses and connection logs—for up to six months.While Ottawa introduced amendments barring orders that create a "systemic vulnerability," tech leaders and cybersecurity experts contend the language is overly vague. Cryptographers and privacy advocates have long maintained that it is impossible to build a "backdoor" exclusively for police without leaving that same entry point exposed to cybercriminals and foreign intelligence agencies.The primary flashpoint is Part 2 of the bill, which grants ministers in the country the authority to issue confidential orders forcing service providers to build interception capabilities for police. The legislation also empowers the government to require companies to retain sensitive customer metadata—including IP addresses and connection logs—for up to six months.While Ottawa introduced amendments prohibiting orders that create a "systemic vulnerability," tech leaders and cryptographers argue the language is dangerously vague. Security experts maintain that creating a "backdoor" for law enforcement inevitably creates a weak point that malicious hackers and foreign spies will eventually exploit.Meta is far from alone in its opposition, joining a broad coalition of tech giants, privacy-focused apps, and digital rights advocates pushing back against the draft law. Both Google and Apple have issued warnings that Bill C-22 threatens customer security and could break end-to-end encryption.Encrypted messaging platform Signal too has stated that it would leave Canada rather than compromise its security protocols, while Toronto-based VPN provider Windscribe pledged to maintain its strict no-logs policy regardless of the bill's outcome.
Article Summary: Canadian lawmakers are considering Bill C-22, which would require electronic service providers to hand over user data to investigators. Critics say the mandate directly threatens end-to-end encryption, which is the security standard used by platforms like WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram.

Article Title: ‘Let Students Search’: Google employees want an AI-free option for schools, here’s why
Article Text:
‘Let Students Search’: Google workers want an AI-free option for schools, here’s why

What Google workers are asking for

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Can schools turn off AI inside Search

Hundreds of Google employees have signed a petition asking the company to give schools a version of Google Search without generative AI. The appeal comes as three of the largest US school districts weigh switching search engines, according to The New York Times. The issue is whether schools can turn off AI for students and still let them look things up on Google.The dispute began earlier this month when Google’s vice president for education, Chris Phillips, told the Times that Search and AI were “deeply integrated”. He said students attempting to use Search at schools that ban AI would see a message saying the service was unavailable. Some districts, including New York City, have already restricted student-facing generative AI over concerns about how it affects learning.New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of using its market power to push AI into public schools. In Chicago, parents, teachers and students protested outside a Google office. The Times subsequently reported that New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago were all considering alternative search engines.The Alphabet Workers Union’s petition, titled “Let Students Search”, is addressed to Phillips, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Search chief Elizabeth Hamon Reid. The union argues that educators should decide when students use AI and that taking away Search could prompt districts to drop other Google products.It also warned that losing school district business could affect job security.“The decision of how and when to implement AI into a classroom belongs to the educators leading it,” Parul Koul, the union’s president and a Google software engineer, said in a statement.Google has said that under changes expected early next year, schools will be able to enable or disable Search, Gemini and NotebookLM individually. That means a school could switch off the standalone Gemini chatbot and keep Search available to students. Google’s clarification left open whether schools could also disable the generative AI features that appear within Search itself.The union said some coverage had made it sound as though Google was deliberately punishing schools for opting out of AI. Its petition asks for a setting that would let schools apply their classroom AI policies to Search while keeping the search engine available for everyday use.
Article Summary: Hundreds of Google employees have signed a petition asking the company to give schools a version of Google Search without generative AI. The appeal comes as three of the largest US school districts weigh switching search engines. The issue is whether schools can turn off AI for students and still let them look things up on Google.

Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna back $165 million fund to help countries manage foreign aid cuts

Why governments are struggling to maintain health services

Where the grant money will be directed

Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz and his wife Cari Tuna are backing a $165 million philanthropic effort aimed at helping countries cope with shrinking international health assistance. The initiative comes as governments face mounting pressure to maintain healthcare programmes that have depended on funding from overseas donors, including services for infectious diseases and other essential medical needs. Through their foundation, Good Ventures, the couple are joining the Livelihood Impact Fund and another private donor in supporting the Health Aid Transition Fund. Announced by Coefficient Giving, the initiative plans to recommend at least $130 million in grants over its first three years, alongside technical support to help governments reorganise health spending and take greater responsibility for services previously financed through foreign aid.The Health Aid Transition Fund was announced on September 18, 2026, by Coefficient Giving, a philanthropic organisation that advises donors and supports initiatives addressing global challenges. Its purpose is to help low- and middle-income countries adjust to a sharp reduction in external financial assistance, particularly in healthcare.The initiative has backing from three sources: Good Ventures, the philanthropic foundation established by Moskovitz and Tuna; the Livelihood Impact Fund; and an additional private donor.Coefficient Giving will oversee the grantmaking process and recommend at least $130 million in grants during the fund's first three years. The wider initiative is valued at $165 million.The money is intended to help governments make decisions about which health services they can continue funding themselves, where spending needs to be redirected and how to make better use of the resources that remain available.Reportedly, International assistance fell by more than 20% between 2024 and 2025, with further reductions expected. Health aid could be more than 25% below its 2024 level by 2030, according to projections included in the fund's announcement.For countries that have relied on overseas donors for years, the change presents an immediate financial challenge. Programs covering HIV/AIDS, malaria and other basic healthcare needs have often depended on external organisations to pay for medicines, manage supply chains, maintain data systems and support medical staff. Governments are now being asked to assume more of these responsibilities, sometimes without having the financial arrangements or personnel in place to do so.The fund's approach extends beyond providing money to cover immediate budget shortages. A significant part of its work will involve technical assistance, giving governments access to financial expertise, research and practical support as they reorganise healthcare spending.This could include helping ministries assess the cost of existing programmes, identify services that need priority funding and determine how much money is required to maintain them. The initiative also plans to support governments in bringing in local organisations to take over responsibilities previously handled by international contractors. Training healthcare workers, improving supply chains and strengthening health information systems are among the other areas identified.Another concern is ensuring that money already allocated to healthcare actually reaches hospitals, clinics and the communities that need it. The fund intends to address weaknesses in public financial management, including fragmented funding arrangements and budget systems that can prevent governments from spending money effectively.Moskovitz's involvement in the initiative comes against a longer history of giving. He co-founded Facebook in 2004 and later established Good Ventures with Tuna. The foundation was set up in 2011 and works with Coefficient Giving to distribute philanthropic grants.The couple signed the Giving Pledge in 2010, committing to donate or give away most of their wealth during their lifetimes or through their wills. In their pledge letter, Moskovitz described the financial rewards from Facebook's growth as a resource that could be directed towards helping others. He also credited Tuna with sharing his commitment to philanthropy.Their stated priorities included supporting a safer, healthier and more economically empowered global community. The letter also described an intention to combine timely giving with careful consideration of where their contributions could make the greatest difference.Good Ventures has since supported work across several areas of international development, including malaria prevention, infectious diseases and broader healthcare initiatives. The OECD's 2026 profile of the foundation recorded $203.4 million in cross-border development funding in 2024, with health and population programmes accounting for a substantial share of its development spending.The new initiative also builds on work that was underway before its formal launch. Coefficient Giving said it had already made approximately $18 million in related grants, much of it directed towards technical teams helping governments respond to funding reductions.The organisation expects the larger fund to expand that work. Although technical advice and government support will account for much of its activity, grants may also go towards delivering healthcare services directly in situations where philanthropic funding can help unlock bilateral assistance that would otherwise remain unused.For the governments involved, the coming years will involve decisions about how much responsibility they can take on themselves and how to finance services that have historically depended on international donors. The Health Aid Transition Fund is intended to support that process over its initial three-year period, as countries work towards health systems with greater domestic funding and control. The initiative also reflects a wider shift in global health financing, with increasing emphasis on helping lower-income countries build sustainable, domestically funded healthcare systems. Its long-term impact will depend on whether governments can maintain essential medical services, strengthen public health infrastructure and replace lost international funding without leaving vulnerable communities behind.
Article Summary: Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna back $165 million fund to help countries manage foreign aid cuts. Initiative comes as governments face mounting pressure to maintain healthcare programmes that have depended on funding from overseas donors. International assistance fell by more than 20% between 2024 and 2025, with further reductions expected.

Article Title: Microsoft 365 outage: Company blames a 'triple' failure for 24-hour-plus global Outlook disruption; Microsoft EVP Charles Lamanna says: Three main factors that...
Article Text:
Microsoft explains its global outage

A July bug slipped past Microsoft 365's load testing

A Teams failover and 14% missing capacity exposed the bug

Outlook stayed down longest because Exchange Online could not switch gateways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft has explained what disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online and a string of other Microsoft 365 services for more than 24 hours last week, and the answer is not one fault but three. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up on November 12. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive at the worst point.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, detailed the root cause of the Microsoft 365 outage in a post on X on Monday. "The incident on Thursday, November 12th, 2026, was caused by three main factors that together caused a global outage for the networking gateway that fronts many Microsoft 365 services," he wrote. He also apologised: "We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations. "The first factor was a latent defect. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal process left servers overwhelmed and unresponsive.The bug came from a fix built specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Lamanna said neither the defect nor that fix applies to broader Windows deployments.The change began rolling out in July, cleared safe deployment, reached servers worldwide over several weeks and ran for more than three months without trouble.So why did testing miss it? Microsoft's load tests leaned on its weaker hardware with fewer cores, while the contention problem gets worse on newer machines with more cores. The test labs' traffic and hardware mix did not match the live fleet.Microsoft runs two independent network gateway systems inside Microsoft 365, so services can move between them during disruptions. About 15 hours before the outage, Teams failed over from the alternative gateway to the "primary" one, which also handles Exchange Online. The company calls this routine, but it added load and changed traffic patterns on that gateway.At the same time, nearly 14% of the gateway's server capacity was out of service because of an unrelated issue from the day before. That alone caused no harm, since the service had enough headroom.Together, though, the extra load and thinner capacity triggered the July bug during peak US traffic hours. Requests piled up until servers stopped responding. Microsoft's traffic management then moved users to healthy endpoints, as designed, which simply spread the same load across fewer machines. In under two hours, the defect had hit servers across the fleet.A separate issue meant the bulkheads between regional "capacity units" also failed to contain the damage, letting a gateway problem become a global outage.Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps could move off the faulty infrastructure, which is why they came back sooner. Teams chats and meetings worked for most of the outage. Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, could not make that switch.Recovery was a fight of its own. Servers returning to service were flooded by queued traffic and went down again. Microsoft's automated recovery systems were not designed for such a broad failure, and because the bug was months old, the usual rollback, flighting and feature flag tools could not quickly reverse it. Even the company's status updates during the outage said it had "not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact.Engineers eventually built an update that returned the code path to its last known good state. They then pulled groups of servers out of service, applied the fix and restarted them, in some cases more than half a region at a time.Microsoft first flagged the problem at 11:24 pm IST on November 12, for users in the Americas, before it spread to at least 70 countries and hit Copilot, government offices, courts and hospitals. In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air reported problems with their customer-support email systems, while OpenAI and Anthropic flagged issues with their Microsoft 365 integrations. The Microsoft executive had already ruled out foul play on November 13, writing, "This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling. "A final Post-Incident Review (PIR) is due later this week. It should also shed light on the separate issue that let the failure jump across regions, which Monday's summary leaves unexplained.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 went down for more than 24 hours on November 12. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive.

Article Title: Another suspected FBI hack, this time involving one of America’s most important crime databases
Article Text:
FBI hacked again? Hackers reportedly accessed the National Crime Information Center, a database used by US police for criminal records, warrants and background checks.

FBI hack: Critical law enforcement system targeted

FBI Director Kash Patel touts cyber efforts

Experts warn of potential risks

Second breach in months

The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a suspected cyberattack targeting its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), one of the country's most important law enforcement databases. As reported by CNN, the data breach was discovered in recently and it involved unauthorised access to a system relied upon by federal, state and local enforcement agencies across the United States. The system holds records on crime victims, missing people and people protected by court orders, as well as suspects, so a breach could affect people who have never been arrested. The reports so far do not say what data, if any, was accessed or who is behind the intrusion.The report further adds that NCIC database which offer nationwide information-sharing network enables the law enforcement agencies to access and exchange data on arrest warrants, criminal histories and background checks. The system is said to be an important operational tool for police departments and federal agencies. A compromise of the system is said to a major cybersecurity concern for FBI. The report suggests that the investigators are still working to find out the scope of the intrusion and whether any information was accessed or altered.The said data breach surfaced shortly after FBI Director Kash Patel gave an interview to Fox News highlighting the cybersecurity initiatives at FBI. During the interview, Patel discussed Operation Winter Shield, a programme designed to encourage organisations to strengthen their systems and prevent cybercriminals from gaining access to sensitive information. He further emphasised that the present administration had taken steps to improve protections for critical infrastructure.Former FBI officials cited by CNN warned that the NCIC system plays a central role in daily law enforcement operations. Officers across the country use the database to identify wanted individuals, check outstanding warrants and access information that can directly affect public and officer safety. As a result, experts say concerns extend beyond the possible theft of sensitive information to the integrity and accuracy of records stored within the system.This is the second data breach that FBI has faced in months. In September this year, A notorious cybercrime group known as ShinyHunters has claimed responsibility for stealing more than 2 terabytes of data from FBI systems, including detailed personal information about thousands of employees and job applicants, according to a report by Axios. The group posted on its dark‑web site that it had obtained “very sensitive data on almost ALL FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.” According to ShinyHunters, the stolen data includes names, agent statuses, emails, phone numbers, home addresses, Social Security numbers, and even spouse information. While cybercriminals and state-sponsored hackers have been infiltrating US IT systems for years, cyber experts told Axios that stealing sensitive personal data specifically about FBI employees marks a notably bold escalation. The concern isn't just the breach itself — it's what happens next. Stolen data of this kind is routinely traded on the dark web, effectively putting it up for sale to whichever buyer is willing to pay the most.
Article Summary: US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a suspected cyberattack targeting its National Crime Information Center (NCIC) The system holds records on crime victims, missing people and people protected by court orders, as well as suspects. The reports so far do not say what data, if any, was accessed or who is behind the intrusion.

Article Title: Canada extends international student arrivals target to 2029; what has changed and what not
Article Text:
What has changed

What has not changed

The gap between targets and arrivals

Sector welcomes stability

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Student numbers remain below targets

Canada has extended its target of welcoming up to 150,000 new international student arrivals a year through 2029, maintaining a cap first outlined in its previous immigration plan as part of a broader effort to keep immigration levels predictable and sustainable. The move comes under the country's new 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan released by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). The updated plan keeps annual temporary resident arrival targets unchanged at 370,000 for each of the next three years. Within that total, Canada will continue to admit up to 150,000 new international students and 220,000 workers annually in 2027, 2028 and now 2029One of the biggest change is the extension of the student arrivals target by an additional year. The previous immigration plan of Canada has already set the 150,000 international student arrivals target for 2027 and 2028. However, the new plan now carries the same target ahead to 2029, offering longer planning horizon to educational institutions. Along with this, the government has also released a three-year immigration roadmap which maintain the annual targets of 380,000 permanent resident admissions through 2029.Along with this, it also introduces measures which are designed to transition some temporary residents already living in Canada to permanent residency. Canada is also planning to increase the number of admissions via programmes such as as the Provincial Nominee Program and Atlantic Immigration Program and the country will also continue reforms to economic immigration and Express Entry selection to better align immigration with labour market needs.The student target sits inside a wider cap of 370,000 new temporary resident arrivals a year, which also includes 220,000 new workers. Permanent resident admissions are held at 380,000 a year, with the economic class staying above 64% of the total. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) says the targets match last year’s plan and support its aim of slowing population growth so housing and services can catch up. It also wants permanent admissions below 1% of the population beyond 2027.The extension comes as Canada falls well short of its existing limits. IRCC’s annual report to Parliament shows 115,180 student arrivals in 2025 against a target of 305,900. Total temporary arrivals were 323,995, below the 604,900 to 742,400 range set for the year. Study permits that became effective, which include extensions, fell 26.1% to 381,725.India remains the largest source country, with 94,025 study permits, or 24.6% of the total. Student transitions to permanent residence fell 18.7% to 20,790.The Canadian Bureau for International Education (CBIE) welcomed the decision, saying stable targets would provide institutions with greater certainty when planning recruitment strategies and programme offerings. CBIE President and CEO Larissa Bezo said the longer-term targets would help institutions work with governments and industry to meet Canada's student arrival goals.Universities Canada also backed the move, arguing that predictable immigration policies are essential for rebuilding confidence in the country's international education sector and attracting global talent.Despite extending the target, Canada remains well below its current student arrival goals. According to the federal government's 2026 Annual Report to Parliament on Immigration, Canada recorded 115,180 international student arrivals in 2025, significantly below the 2025 target of 305,900 student arrivals. Overall temporary resident arrivals also fell short of target levels. For Indian students, Canada remains a major destination despite recent policy tightening. Government data shows India was the largest source country for study permits that became effective in 2025, accounting for 94,025 permits, ahead of China and Nigeria.
Article Summary: Canada has extended its target of welcoming up to 150,000 new international student arrivals a year through 2029. The move comes under the country's new 2027-2029 Immigration Levels Plan released by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) The extension comes as Canada falls well short of its existing limits. Despite extending the target, Canada remains well below its current student arrival goals.

Article Title: Dario Amodei to Jamie Dimon: At Anthropic we do not hire deeply technically talented people to make sure our culture is ...
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Who Anthropic refuses to hire

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A few days ahead of Anthropic’s $1.4 trillion initial public offering (IPO), company CEO Dario Amodei sat down with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon to explain the strict hiring philosophy that has kept the artificial intelligence (AI) company unified – even when it means turning away brilliant engineers. According to Amodei, prioritising company culture over raw technical ability has been a non-negotiable rule since the very beginning. Amodei explained that when he and his six co-founders left their previous company to launch Anthropic, they made an agreement on day one to put talent and culture first – a priority so central that Amodei still spends much of his own time on it.“From day one, myself and the other six co-founders said, ‘we're going to focus on talent, and we're going to focus on culture. And right from the beginning, we set things up in such a way that we have a culture interview that everyone goes through, and we've been very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented, but who don’t fit our culture,” Amodei told Dimon.To protect how its teams work together, Anthropic enforces clear boundaries during its mandatory culture interviews. Amodei explained that the company actively screens out candidates who fall into three specific categories: “Jerks, spotlight-stealers and those who have no indifference to public benefit”.He admitted that passing up top technical talent hurts in the short run. However, he emphasised that sticking to those standards consistently pays off by creating a workplace where everyone is on the same side.“We don't want people who are jerks. We don't want people who try to steal the show and don't work well with others. We don’t want people who aren’t oriented towards the public benefit, and it turns out if you stick to that consistently, it's painful in the short run, but you get a team where everyone works together, and everyone is on the same side,” the Anthropic CEO explained.“One of the things that most causes difficulty for companies is if you have an incredible team, but people aren't working together, they're working against each other, you have this team that works against that team that works against the third team, and they spend all of their energy fighting each other,” he added.Notably, all 7 co-founders are still at the company, and two senior product people quit and came back within two weeks.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei tells JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon about the company's strict hiring philosophy. He says the company screens out candidates who fall into three specific categories: “Jerks, spotlight-stealers and those who have no indifference to public benefit”

What are UK consumers' rights when an online delivery goes missing?

A customer in London was left without a £544 smartphone and out of pocket after an Amazon delivery went missing, with the company's tracking system indicating that the package might be lost. When he requested a refund, Amazon's customer service process reportedly led to his order being registered as a return, even though he maintained that the phone had never arrived. The situation became more complicated when Amazon had already collected two monthly installments of £108, amounting to £216. After encountering difficulties resolving the issue through the company's customer service channels, the customer approached The Guardian. Following the newspaper's intervention, Amazon issued a refund within four hours and offered him an additional £50 voucher.The incident was reported by The Guardian on January 12, 2026, in its consumer affairs coverage. The customer, identified only as SH, had ordered a smartphone worth £544 through Amazon UK.When the delivery failed to arrive, Amazon's tracking system indicated that the package might be lost and gave him the option of requesting a refund.However, when he contacted customer service, he was reportedly told to wait another seven days before proceeding with the claim.After waiting, SH attempted to submit an incident report as instructed. Amazon asked him to use the email address associated with his account, but the report was rejected because the email allegedly did not meet the company's security requirements.The customer then tried using an alternative email address, but Amazon would not accept it because it was not linked to his account. This left him unable to complete the incident-report process through either route.The problem escalated when his Amazon order page showed that he had requested to return the phone. It stated that a refund would be issued once the product was sent back, despite his repeated assertion that the device had never been delivered.This effectively left him facing a return requirement for an item he said he did not possess.The financial implications added to the customer's frustration. The £544 smartphone was being paid for in monthly instalments of £108, and Amazon had already collected the first two payments, amounting to £216.The customer was therefore left paying for a product he said he had never received while trying to navigate the company's refund and verification procedures. The Guardian report did not specify whether any further instalments were collected during the dispute.It also did not identify the smartphone model or disclose the financing provider involved in the instalment arrangement.After encountering difficulties resolving the issue through Amazon's customer service channels, SH sought assistance from The Guardian.Following the newspaper's intervention, Amazon issued the refund within four hours. The company also offered him a £50 voucher as a goodwill gesture.Responding to the complaint, Amazon said: "We are sorry for the inconvenience our mistake has caused."The company did not provide a detailed public explanation of why its system had recorded a return request for a phone the customer said he had never received or why the verification process had prevented him from completing his claim.The incident also raises questions about consumer protection when online purchases fail to arrive. Under the UK's Consumer Rights Act 2015, retailers are generally responsible for goods until they come into the physical possession of the customer or someone authorised by them to receive the delivery.Section 28 of the Act requires retailers to deliver goods without undue delay and, unless another delivery period has been agreed, within 30 days. If a retailer fails to meet the applicable delivery obligations, consumers may have the right to cancel the order and obtain a refund, depending on the circumstances.Section 29 establishes that the risk of loss or damage generally remains with the retailer until the consumer takes physical possession of the goods. An exception applies where the consumer independently commissions a carrier that was not offered as an option by the retailer.This means that when a retailer arranges delivery and a parcel goes missing before reaching the customer, responsibility generally remains with the retailer.
Article Summary: A customer in London was left without a £544 smartphone and out of pocket after an Amazon delivery went missing. Amazon's tracking system indicated that the package might be lost. When he requested a refund, Amazon's customer service process reportedly led to his order being registered as a return, even though he maintained that the phone had never arrived. Amazon had already collected two monthly installments of £108, amounting to £216.

Article Title: US government shakes up cyber leadership days after tech outages hit flights, banks and key government systems

Kirsten Davies, Chief Information Officer of the Department of War

What was the reason for outages

Who is Kirsten Davies

Who is Sean Cairncross

US President Donald Trump has replaced the country’s national cyber director just days after a wave of tech outages grounded flights and disrupted email, banking and national security systems. Sean Cairncross, who has held the role since August 2025, will be succeeded by Kirsten Davies, the chief information officer at the Department of War. According to a report by The Financial Times, the change comes while the White House is under pressure over how it manages cyber security, and over the new threat posed by advanced AI tools.The national cyber director oversees cyber security policy and strategy across the federal government. The president appoints the director, but the Senate has to confirm the choice, the report said. Last week, computer systems and online tools at several organisations went down, including Microsoft, JPMorgan, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Security Agency (NSA). The outages caused widespread disruption and panic.Denying any speculation about cyber terrorism, US officials have said the incidents were caused by organisations racing to patch software bugs.AI tools have changed how such bugs are found. They can analyse huge amounts of computer code at great speed and spot flaws and fixes far faster than any human. This has set off a cyber security arms race, as organisations try to find and patch weaknesses before hackers can exploit them. Some officials claimed that the digital systems are using old equipment that was unable to share the increased load.Davies was confirmed by the Senate for her current role at the Pentagon. Earlier in her career, she held senior cyber security roles in the private sector at companies including Siemens, Barclays and Unilever. In a statement on X, she said the US needs to modernise its digital infrastructure.“Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come . . . but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future,” she said.Cairncross told CNN he was proud of his work “to strengthen America’s cyber security, protect our critical infrastructure, confront foreign threats, and position America to lead the world in super intelligence”. He is a longtime official at the Republican National Committee and worked at the White House during Trump’s first term. He is a lawyer by training and had little direct cyber security experience before Trump appointed him last year, the FT reported.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos pledged $10 billion for climate action by 2030; his Earth Fund has now announced over $100 million for Amazon rainforest protection, including Indigenous territories and wildfire prevention
Article Text:
Bezos Earth Fund directs fresh funding towards Amazon conservation

Protecting 37 million acres through Indigenous-led conservation efforts

$15 million allocated to tackle Amazon deforestation and wildfires

Satellites, artificial intelligence and DNA to monitor the rainforest

How previous Amazon grants have supported millions of acres

Bezos faces a $10 billion giving target by 2030

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Amazon rainforest is facing mounting pressure from deforestation, fires and the gradual deterioration of its ecosystems. Against this backdrop, Jeff Bezos ’ philanthropic organisation has announced a fresh funding package worth more than $100 million for conservation work across the region. As reported by Fortune, the investment comes as the billionaire approaches a deadline attached to a climate commitment he made in 2020, when he pledged to distribute $10 billion towards environmental causes by 2030. The latest grants will support projects in several South American countries, with funding directed towards Indigenous communities, forest restoration, wildfire prevention and technologies designed to monitor changes across the vast rainforest.The Bezos Earth Fund, established by Jeff Bezos in 2020, is distributing the money through 15 grants covering different aspects of rainforest protection. Lauren Sánchez Bezos, who is married to the Amazon founder, serves as the organisation's vice chair. “We were drawn to the region because the Amazon rainforest is one of the most important areas for biodiversity and crucial in the global fight against climate change,” said Cristián Samper, managing director and head of nature solutions.The funding package is among the larger investments made by the organisation in a single conservation effort. The rainforest is also home to millions of people and plays a significant role in regulating the global climate.The region has experienced extensive forest loss. According to the World Wildlife Fund's 2022 report, approximately 17% of Amazon forests have been converted to other uses, while another 17% have been degraded. A 2024 study published in the journal Nature, titled ‘ Critical transitions in the Amazon forest system ’ raised concerns about the longer-term outlook. It estimated that by 2050, as much as 47% of the Amazon's forests could face multiple environmental pressures severe enough to push parts of the ecosystem towards a tipping point.The biggest allocation in the new funding round is $46 million, earmarked for the protection of forests and Indigenous territories. Among the organisations and groups receiving support are FUNBIO, the International Conservation Fund of Canada, the Kayapó Indigenous Alliance and the Amazon Conservation Team. The Amazon Basin is home to approximately 400 Indigenous peoples, representing more than two million people, according to information cited by the Earth Fund. Their territories cover extensive areas of rainforest, and the organisation points to Indigenous-managed forests as some of the best-preserved parts of the region.The grants are intended to strengthen community-led conservation, including the protection of territories and the resources needed to monitor them. Samper said Indigenous groups were particularly well placed to identify threats and respond to problems because they live on and manage the land. This part of the programme is also connected to the fund's longer-term targets. It wants to help protect an additional 37 million acres of land and improve management systems across another 285 million acres.Reportedly, more than $15 million has been set aside for work addressing deforestation and wildfires. Leonardo DiCaprio's environmental organisation, Re:wild, is among the recipients. Cattle ranching and fires are two of the main pressures identified by the Earth Fund. Forest is frequently cleared to create grazing land, with burning used as part of the process. Fires can then spread beyond the intended areas, damaging surrounding vegetation and making restoration more difficult.The organisation wants its supported projects to help reduce annual deforestation by approximately 220,000 acres. Early detection is a particular focus. Samper said identifying fires before they spread can significantly limit the damage, which has led the fund to increase its support for monitoring and response systems. The work builds on the Earth Fund's backing for FireSat, a satellite initiative designed to track wildfires around the world. The project uses a network of satellites to identify fires and monitor their development, including in the Amazon Basin.A further $19 million will support monitoring projects across Amazon. The grants include work by the Andes Amazon Fund and the Natural Assets Laboratory of the Spatial Informatics Group. Some of the projects will combine different technologies to build a more detailed picture of the rainforest's condition. One initiative, called Amazon.ia, will bring together environmental DNA collected from water and soil, acoustic recording equipment, AI-enabled cameras and high-resolution satellite images.The aim is to make it easier to follow changes in wildlife populations and ecosystems without relying entirely on expensive, traditional monitoring methods. Three grants will support the development of tools intended to lower the cost of tracking species and ecological changes.Restoration is another part of the package. Fortune reported, a $2 million grant to the International Institute for Sustainability will establish two experimental sites covering a combined 12,000 acres. Researchers will use these locations to test different approaches to restoring damaged forest areas. The Earth Fund also wants to use satellite information and other monitoring systems to assess whether protected forests remain intact, whether deforestation is declining and whether degraded land is recovering.The latest announcement adds to a conservation programme that has been running since 2021. According to the Bezos Earth Fund, it has awarded approximately $150 million for Amazon-related projects over the past five years, working with more than 40 organisations across five South American countries. The organisation says its earlier funding has helped establish 16 million acres of new conservation areas and secure legal recognition for 14 million acres of Indigenous territories. It also reports improvements in the management of existing protected areas and Indigenous lands covering approximately 450 million acres.The fund has identified early intervention, particularly in the case of wildfires, as an area where philanthropic support can make a difference. Its latest grants are intended to build on those earlier projects rather than operate as a separate conservation programme.The Amazon investment comes as the Earth Fund works towards the commitment Bezos announced in February 2020. At the time, he pledged $10 billion over 10 years to support scientists, activists and organisations working on climate change and environmental protection. The deadline is now approaching. Figures reported by Fortune in September 2026 put the fund's total grants at approximately $2.4 billion. That leaves close to $7 billion to be distributed over the remaining period before 2030.The organisation has continued announcing sizeable commitments in recent months. These include more than $25 million for ocean conservation projects in the Pacific and a separate $100 million commitment as a founding member of the Species Recovery Alliance, which focuses on animals facing extinction risks. Earlier in 2026, the fund also committed $34 million towards the development of more sustainable clothing materials, an initiative led by Lauren Sánchez Bezos.The latest environmental grants were announced days after Bezos disclosed the transfer of 771,492 Amazon shares to nonprofit organisations. The shares were valued at approximately $200 million, according to filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, as reported by Fortune.A separate filing showed that the Bezos Earth Fund Foundation received 97,404 of those shares.Samper said the organisation would assess its conservation work through reports from grant recipients and independent satellite analysis. Its monitoring will examine forest cover, deforestation rates, restoration progress and the management of protected territories.
Article Summary: The Bezos Earth Fund, established by Jeff Bezos in 2020, is distributing the money through 15 grants covering different aspects of rainforest protection. It wants to help protect an additional 37 million acres of land and improve management systems across another 285 million acres. The investment comes as the billionaire approaches a deadline attached to a climate commitment he made in 2020.

Article Title: Why this WhatsApp rival is blocking screenshots to keep Apple, Google out of your chats
Article Text:
Signal is turning off screenshots on iPhone and Android, and AI is the reason

End-to-end encryption does not cover what Siri AI and Gemini read off your screen

Meta ’s Muse AI agent has already reached into Signal chats through accessibility settings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support Signal's decision to block screenshots to protect user privacy? Yes, privacy is paramount No, this limits functionality 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Signal will now stop you from taking screenshots inside its app on iPhones and Android phones, and you are not the one it is worried about. The privacy-focused WhatsApp rival says the block is meant to keep AI assistants such as Apple ’s Siri AI and Google ’s Gemini from reading your private chats straight off the screen. The protection is switched on by default on iOS 27, and on Android versions where Signal can detect an AI assistant trying to scan the display. Anyone who wants screenshots back can turn it off in settings, though Signal warns this exposes their chats, and their contacts’, to these agents.In a blog post on November 20, Signal president Meredith Whittaker said AI features built into phone operating systems are weakening the app’s ability to guarantee privacy on its own. She called this deep integration of agents “an existential threat to Signal”.On iPhones, the new toggle appears in Signal’s settings as Block Siri AI. On Android, the app turns on its existing Screen security option when it spots an assistant trying to read the screen. Users also get a pop-up offering to lift the block.Signal’s encryption protects messages as they travel between phones. It cannot do much once an assistant scans an open chat.According to Signal, that captured content can then sit in a local database or move to whichever server the agent relies on, well outside the app’s control. The company says it spent months running forensic checks on Android and iOS to learn what these systems do with app data.Signal admits the fix is incomplete. Blocking screenshots does nothing to stop agents from pulling data stored on the phone through the file system. It also cannot offer the same protection on macOS, since operating system makers give developers no easy way to restrict AI access without hurting how an app works.Signal also flagged third-party agents such as Meta’s Muse, which it says lean on deep accessibility permissions users grant during setup. Reuters reported earlier this week that Muse pulled Signal messages on a Mac and on an Android phone this way. On the Mac, it combined accessibility and screenshot tools to capture the chats and extract the text. An Apple update this week closed that specific route. Meta has said Muse can access other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant.Signal has done this before. Last year, it used the same screenshot block on Windows 11 to keep Microsoft’s Recall feature from saving its chats.Signal, run by the non-profit Signal Technology Foundation, is now asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for two things. The first is a simple, documented way for developers to opt their apps out of AI access, covering screen reading, file access, notifications and other system tools. The second is clear documentation on how these AI agents access and process data. Signal says Google and Apple have begun talking to it about how their AI systems should work with privacy-focused apps.
Article Summary: Signal will now stop you from taking screenshots inside its app on iPhones and Android phones. The privacy-focused WhatsApp rival says the block is meant to keep AI assistants such as Apple ’s Siri AI and Google’s Gemini from reading your private chats straight off the screen. Anyone who wants screenshots back can turn it off in settings.

Article Title: Days after Sundar Pichai congratulated Elon Musk’s space company, Google picks SpaceX-rival to launch AI computing satellites in 2029
Article Text:
Tech giants looking to move power-hungry AI data centers beyond Earth

In-house AI hardware:

Near-continuous sunlight:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jeff Bezos’s space venture Blue Origin and Alphabet’s Google have partnered with the latter has chosen the New Glenn rocket to carry satellites into orbit for Project Suncatcher, an initiative designed to run artificial intelligence (AI) systems in space. Scheduled for the first quarter of 2029, the mission will serve as Google’s first heavy-lift flight dedicated to Project Suncatcher, sending multiple computing satellites aboard New Glenn. The agreement also hands Blue Origin a high-profile future contract for New Glenn as the company works to grow its launch business following earlier delays and a launchpad explosion in May.The partnership announcement comes days after Google CEO Sundar Pichai congratulated SpaceX and its CEO Elon Musk after the company achieved its first-ever midair catch of a Starship spacecraft – a reusable upper-stage spacecraft and super heavy-lift launch system – returning from space. Pichai said the achievement “still feels like science fiction” and added that watching the event live was incredible.As surging AI adoption drives up demand for computing power and strains terrestrial electricity grids, land and cooling systems, tech and space companies, including Elon Musk’s SpaceX and startup Starcloud, are exploring orbital data centers as an alternative. Google’s upcoming mission aims to test whether continuous solar power in space can support heavy AI workloads:Each satellite will be equipped with Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs), custom chips engineered to run AI models, packing roughly the computing capacity of a full server rack in a traditional ground-based data center.The spacecraft will be placed into an orbit that will have near-constant sunlight to evaluate how effectively solar energy can power sustained computing off-planet.Notably, the efforts are built on an earlier SpaceX prototype flight. In October, Google and Planet Labs launched the first Project Suncatcher prototype aboard a SpaceX rocket, later confirming the satellite was functioning as expected after making contact.The 2029 Blue Origin mission builds on groundwork already underway.That initial test flight is examining how Google’s chips hold up against intense launch forces, space radiation, and extreme temperature swings, while helping engineers figure out how to manage heat without Earth’s natural airflow.Meanwhile, engineering and cost challenges remain. For example, space radiation can degrade electronics and corrupt data, while heat generated by high-powered chips must be dissipated using specialised pipes and panels instead of standard cooling fans or liquid systems.Industry experts have pointed out that steep launch expenses, complex engineering demands and limited satellite manufacturing capacity mean commercial orbital data centers are likely still years away.
Article Summary: Project Suncatcher aims to test whether continuous solar power in space can support heavy AI workloads. Each satellite will be equipped with Google’s tensor processing units (TPUs), custom chips engineered to run AI models. The spacecraft will be placed into an orbit that will have near-constant sunlight.

What should students and alumni check

Microsoft is phasing out free student and alumni email service. The company says it will retire Office 365 A1, the Student Use Benefit program and its free Exchange Online for Alumni offer on January 1, 2028. Schools, colleges and universities with an active enrollment that began before that date can keep using those licenses until the end of their current term.For students who receive coursework and campus notices at a school address, and graduates who still use a university inbox, the timing depends on when their institution’s agreement ends. Schools that want to keep those Microsoft-hosted mailboxes will need to move users to an eligible paid license. Institutions that switch email providers will need to tell users how and when to access their mail.Office 365 A1 will first reach the end of sale through Microsoft’s partner channels on May 1, 2027. Institutions with a qualifying active enrollment can still add A1 licenses during their existing term. This means a school can continue assigning accounts under that enrollment while it decides how to handle email once the agreement ends.Microsoft’s new education lineup includes a no-cost student plan called Microsoft 365 Education A0. It includes desktop and web versions of Office apps for eligible students. Exchange Online, the service that hosts Microsoft school mailboxes, is available on paid student plans starting with Microsoft 365 Education A2.Microsoft says institutions can assign different licenses to different user groups. A university could buy licenses for students who need Microsoft-hosted email and use the no-cost plan for eligible students whose email is handled by another provider.Microsoft will offer a paid version of Exchange Online for Alumni. Universities that choose to continue providing Microsoft-hosted email to graduates can move them to the paid offer after their current term. Whether a graduate keeps the same address will depend on what the university decides to provide.Students and alumni can ask their institution’s IT department when their current email service is due to change and whether the school plans to keep their address active. If the institution is moving to another provider, users can check whether existing messages and contacts will be transferred and how long they will have access to the old inbox.Graduates who use a university address for job applications, professional contacts or personal accounts may need to update those records if their address is being retired. The same applies to services that send password reset links or verification codes to a school inbox. Those details are easier to change while the account can still receive mail.
Article Summary: Microsoft is phasing out free student and alumni email service.
